title: Completed coefficient reindexing preserves K-flat representatives
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, g : X ≅ Y a scheme isomorphism, and F its recorded completed coefficient module inverse image [def-sf-adic-closed-reindexing-maps, def-weil-proetale-iso-sectionwise-inverse-image]. For every flat-term complex P of completed coefficient modules on Y that is K-flat against all acyclic complexes, the termwise complex F(P) is K-flat against all acyclic completed coefficient complexes on X [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. No residue-characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Step 5, completed coefficient reindexing; Stacks Modules on Sites Tags 03EL and 07A4, and Cohomology on Sites Tag 06YP.

proof.text: The completed inverse image is the exact additive equivalence already constructed from the inverse site equivalence and inverse completed coefficient map, as in the already proved podCompletedInverseImage_equivalence. Exactness of each direction preserves and reflects acyclicity.

Apply the ordinary natural tensor comparison to each total summand. The coproduct universal property gives the signed-total comparison. This is exactly the existing exactTensorTotalIso helper used for semilinear tensor evaluation: naturality intertwines both differentials, additivity preserves the sign, and the right adjoint ensures preservation of the coproducts.

For an acyclic complex Z on X, use the inverse equivalence to obtain an acyclic VZ on Y. K-flatness of P makes (VZ) tensor P acyclic. Exact reindexing preserves this acyclicity, and the signed-total comparison followed by the termwise counit identifies its image with Z tensor FP. Transporting acyclicity along this isomorphism proves the assertion. This also handles zero complexes and the empty site.
